SUMMARY
Quantum gravity exists because our two best theories of nature describe different regimes of reality—and fundamentally disagree when those regimes overlap. At large scales, gravity is described by Einstein’s general relativity, where mass and energy curve spacetime itself. At small scales, the universe is governed by quantum mechanics, which successfully explains atoms,
